global_caption: The video consists of 6 shots and is a tutorial-style demonstration of gardening and planting. It uses a neutral-toned watercolor picture book style, set in a public science garden work area in the museum atrium. The lighting primarily features soft natural diffused light from the glass skylight, supplemented by mild indoor ambient reflection. The overall camera movement is steady and clear. The The emotional tone remains consistently quiet, gentle, and educational in nature.
shot1: Shot 1 begins with a fade-in, using a medium high-angle shot with slight zoom-in. Foreground shows the edge of a wooden workbench, midground focuses on an anthropomorphic lion entering the frame and placing a flowerpot, trowel, and seed packet onto the surface in sequence. Background is softly blurred, showing the museum atrium garden and tall columns. Moderate depth of field clearly highlights the instructional subject. Lighting is soft and even. A distinct table contact The shot ends with a stable view of neatly arranged tools, establishing a clear starting point for the next step.
shot2: Shot 2 follows the previous shot with a hard cut, using a close-up high-angle tight shot. The composition centers on the interior of an empty flowerpot. The foreground briefly captures the claw holding the trowel, while focus clearly tracks the falling stones and soil. First, small stones are laid at the bottom to form a distinct drainage layer, followed by loose nutrient soil being poured in, gradually raising the soil level. Despite the watercolor texture, the material contrast between rolling stones and pouring soil remains clearly distinguishable. The camera performs minimal downward tilt and fixed tracking to ensure viewers accurately observe the sequence.
shot3: Shot 3 transitions via action-matched editing from the prior shot, using a close-up eye-level slightly high-angle shot. The subject first gently levels the soil surface, then uses fingertips or a small tool to press several rows of evenly spaced shallow holes into the top layer. Soil transforms from loose and uneven to flat and orderly, with consistent spacing and depth of holes. Soft daylight maintains stable neutral brightness. Distant museum crowd murmurs persist but remain unobtrusive. The camera follows the hand horizontally, then slightly zooms in, allowing viewers to clearly understand the precision required in soil preparation before sowing.
shot4: Shot 4 cuts sharply from the previous shot, transitioning to a tight close-up high-angle shot. Composition is tighter, focusing on the seed packet opening, hand movements, and shallow hole positions. The anthropomorphic lion plants seeds one by one, each precisely landing in a hole, then gently covers with fine soil and lightly presses the surface with fingertip. The surface changes from visible holes to a softly filled, slightly raised state. Movements are smooth and rhythmically clear. The camera performs a very short zoom-in and pause, allowing “下种—覆土—轻压” three sub-steps to complete fully within a single shot.
shot5: Shot 5 continues into the next phase via a soft fade transition, using a medium-close eye-level shot. Foreground shows a label card and pen, background shows the flowerpot after sowing. The anthropomorphic lion first writes the sowing date on the label, then inserts it into the soil edge. Next, it picks up a narrow-spout watering can and slowly waters the soil thoroughly for the first time. After water falls, soil color gradually darkens, surface changes from loose dry to uniformly moist, with minor local sinking and absorption changes. Lighting remains soft and natural under the skylight. The camera first slightly shifts sideways to capture the date writing, then slowly tilts down to follow the water flow, ensuring both operational details and material changes are clearly visible.
shot6: Shot 6 connects to the previous shot via action-matched editing, cutting to a wide eye-level slightly low-angle shot. Foreground shows the flowerpot steadily held by both hands, midground shows the anthropomorphic lion walking toward a display rack on one side of the museum atrium, background reveals the glass skylight and open space of the public science garden. The subject places the pot under the skylight but not directly exposed to sunlight, and uses hand gestures to indicate maintaining diffused light and occasional watering—completing the final step from sowing to care instructions. Distant crowd murmurs become slightly clearer again. A soft placement The camera smoothly pans with the subject, then gently pulls back, ending the entire tutorial in a calm, tidy, and instructive-completion atmosphere.
